title: High-Speed Low-TTC Following Risk Case
text: In a continuous high-speed following scenario, if the vehicle keeps a high speed under a small forward gap and the closing speed is positive, the minimum TTC will drop rapidly. This type of scenario usually corresponds to hard braking or rear-end near-miss risk, so the vehicle should prioritize deceleration and increase the following distance.
risk_mechanism: Low TTC and short forward spacing jointly compress the following vehicle's reaction time, making a short-horizon rear-end conflict likely.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_car_following, car_following using risk evidence from TTC, THW, headway, relative_speed. Source case: High-Speed Low-TTC Following Risk Case.

title: Persistent Low-TTC Following Risk Case
text: In a high-speed following scenario, the following vehicle continuously approaches the lead vehicle with a high relative speed, keeping TTC at a low level for a long duration. This behavior significantly increases rear-end risk and should be corrected by decelerating to restore a safe gap.
risk_mechanism: When the following vehicle continuously approaches the lead vehicle with a high relative speed, reaction time and braking space are compressed for an extended period, increasing the risk of rear-end collision or hard-braking near-misses.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_car_following, car_following using risk evidence from TTC, THW, headway, relative_speed. Source case: Persistent Low-TTC Following Risk Case.

title: High-Speed Cut-in with Insufficient Rear-Vehicle Reaction Case
text: In a high-speed scenario, if a cut-in vehicle enters the target lane when the available gap is small, the rear vehicle faces significantly shortened reaction time and braking space. If the relative speed is closing and the headway drops abruptly, the interaction should be treated as high risk.
risk_mechanism: A cut-in suddenly shortens the reaction time and braking space of the rear vehicle in the target lane; if the relative motion is still closing, the risk increases.

text: When multiple interaction objects exist simultaneously in a roundabout, a driver who focuses on only one target may overlook approaching vehicles or cyclists from other directions, creating a compound-risk scenario.

text: Near a roundabout exit or side area, a cyclist may be in the driver's visual blind spot. If the vehicle does not decelerate in advance or enlarge the safety margin, a close-distance conflict can easily occur.

title: High-Speed Following Response to Lead-Vehicle Hard Braking Case
text: In high-speed following, if the lead vehicle clearly decelerates and the following vehicle has both low TTC and low THW, it should immediately decelerate and restore a safe time headway.
risk_mechanism: When the lead vehicle suddenly decelerates while the following vehicle is still in short-headway following, the available braking time is rapidly compressed, making a rear-end near-miss likely.

title: High-Speed Traffic Disturbance Amplification Following Case
text: In high-speed traffic flow, if small THW and large relative-speed fluctuations persist across multiple frames, the vehicle should decelerate smoothly and increase following distance to prevent disturbances from amplifying upstream.
risk_mechanism: Short headways in a high-speed vehicle queue amplify minor speed disturbances, causing following vehicles to enter low-safety-margin states repeatedly.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_car_following, car_following using risk evidence from THW, headway, relative_speed. Source case: High-Speed Traffic Disturbance Amplification Following Case.

title: High-Speed Cut-in Causing Rear-Vehicle TTC Drop Case
text: When a vehicle's cut-in would cause a sudden TTC drop for the rear vehicle in the target lane, the lane change should be aborted or delayed instead of forcing the merge.
risk_mechanism: After the cut-in vehicle occupies the target lane, the rear vehicle's forward gap and reaction time suddenly decrease, forcing the rear vehicle to decelerate sharply.

title: High-Speed Cut-in with Insufficient Front and Rear Gaps Case
text: If the available front and rear gaps in the target lane are both small, a high-speed lane change should be delayed or canceled until a more stable safe gap is available.
risk_mechanism: When both front and rear gaps in the target lane are insufficient, continuing the lane change compresses the safety margins of both front and rear vehicles and triggers multi-vehicle chain adjustments.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_cut_in, cut_in using risk evidence from headway. Source case: High-Speed Cut-in with Insufficient Front and Rear Gaps Case.

title: Lane Change with Fast-Approaching Rear Vehicle Case
text: When a vehicle from behind in the target lane approaches with a high relative speed, immediate merging should be avoided even if the current lateral distance appears acceptable.
risk_mechanism: When the rear vehicle in the target lane approaches rapidly, the lane-changing vehicle may misjudge the available gap, leaving the rear vehicle with insufficient reaction space.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_lane_change, lane_change using risk evidence from TTC, headway, relative_speed, lateral_clearance. Source case: Lane Change with Fast-Approaching Rear Vehicle Case.

title: High-Speed Premature Return After Overtaking Case
text: After overtaking at high speed, if the return gap to the overtaken vehicle is insufficient, the vehicle should remain in its lane and return only after increasing the spacing.
risk_mechanism: Returning too early after overtaking compresses the forward space of the overtaken vehicle, turning normal following into short-headway following abruptly.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_lane_change, overtaking_return using risk evidence from TTC, headway, lateral_clearance. Source case: High-Speed Premature Return After Overtaking Case.

title: Urban Intersection Pedestrian Crossing Low-TTC Case
text: At an urban intersection, if a pedestrian approaches the vehicle's predicted path and both TTC and DCPA are low, the vehicle should prioritize yielding and reduce speed.

text: When there is occlusion near an intersection or roadside area and a pedestrian may enter the lane, the vehicle should decelerate in advance and monitor the occluded area.

text: When a motor vehicle overtakes a cyclist, if the lateral clearance and DCPA are too low, it should decelerate and increase lateral spacing instead of passing closely.

text: If a cyclist is parallel to the vehicle and lateral-speed fluctuations are evident, the vehicle should reduce speed and increase lateral distance.
risk_mechanism: In a parallel state, cyclist lateral motion is unstable, and low DCPA can turn a slight deviation into a lateral conflict.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_bicycle using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, lateral_clearance, VRU. Source case: Parallel Cyclist Minor-Drift Conflict Case.

text: When a vehicle turns left or right across a crosswalk and a pedestrian is approaching the conflict point, the vehicle should stop or significantly decelerate to yield.

text: At an unsignalized or complex intersection, when two vehicles' predicted paths cross and their arrival times at the conflict point are close, the vehicle should actively decelerate and yield.

title: Unsignalized Intersection Cyclist Crossing Case
text: At an unsignalized intersection, if a cyclist crosses the vehicle's predicted path, the vehicle should prioritize yielding and reduce speed.

evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_bicycle using risk evidence from TTC, min_future_distance, VRU. Source case: Unsignalized Intersection Cyclist Crossing Case.

text: When a vehicle approaches a roundabout entry at high speed and a vehicle inside the roundabout is already near the conflict point, it should decelerate early and yield.

title: Cyclist Crossing a Roundabout Exit Case
text: If a cyclist crosses the vehicle's exit path at a roundabout exit, the vehicle should stop or significantly decelerate to yield.
risk_mechanism: When a cyclist crosses the exit, the vehicle's exit path and the cyclist's path form a short-horizon crossing conflict at the exit.

title: Roundabout Multi-Vehicle Gap Competition Case
text: When multiple vehicles in a roundabout approach the same conflict area at the same time, the vehicle should avoid occupying the gap aggressively and continuously monitor multiple objects.

title: Roundabout Parallel Motor-Vehicle Lateral Compression Case
text: When parallel vehicles inside a roundabout have insufficient lateral clearance, the vehicle should maintain a stable trajectory and decelerate appropriately to avoid lateral squeezing.
risk_mechanism: Vehicle lateral trajectories vary significantly during curved roundabout driving. If parallel vehicles have insufficient lateral clearance, lateral squeezing risk arises.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_parallel_conflict using risk evidence from min_future_distance, lateral_clearance. Source case: Roundabout Parallel Motor-Vehicle Lateral Compression Case.

title: Roundabout Exit Vehicle Lateral Cut-Out Case
text: When a vehicle cuts from the inner roundabout lane toward the exit and an adjacent vehicle is too close, it should delay exiting and keep its lane stable.

text: If a cyclist near the roundabout entry approaches a lateral conflict area, the vehicle should yield before merging and monitor the cyclist.

title: Pedestrian Hesitant Crossing Near Unprotected Crosswalk Case
text: Near an unprotected crosswalk, a pedestrian crossing slowly or in a stop-and-go manner has unstable intent. The vehicle should decelerate early and yield instead of using a brief gap to pass first.
risk_mechanism: A pedestrian hesitating at low speed near a crosswalk increases trajectory uncertainty. If the vehicle passes with an efficiency-first strategy, a short-horizon lateral crossing conflict can easily form.

title: Slow Vulnerable Pedestrian Crossing High-Risk Case
text: When a slow pedestrian is near the vehicle's predicted path, the vehicle should handle the situation with a more conservative safety margin, yield early, and reduce speed.
risk_mechanism: A slow pedestrian needs a longer clearance time. Even if the current TTC is not extremely low, future path overlap can continuously increase exposure risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_pedestrian using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, min_future_distance, lateral_clearance, VRU. Source case: Slow Vulnerable Pedestrian Crossing High-Risk Case.

title: Multiple Pedestrians Crossing with Occlusion Case
text: In a scenario with multiple pedestrians crossing consecutively, the vehicle should not resume speed immediately just because the nearest pedestrian has left the path; it should confirm that the entire conflict area is clear.
risk_mechanism: When multiple pedestrians cross, pedestrians in front may occlude those behind. Accelerating immediately after yielding to a single target may miss VRUs still in the conflict area.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_pedestrian using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, occlusion, VRU. Source case: Multiple Pedestrians Crossing with Occlusion Case.

title: Cyclist Lateral Avoidance Causing Close-Conflict Case
text: When a cyclist shows an obvious lateral-shift tendency and the lateral spacing is insufficient, the motor vehicle should reduce speed and increase lateral buffer rather than overtaking closely.
risk_mechanism: A cyclist may suddenly shift laterally to avoid roadside obstacles. If a motor vehicle passes closely, DCPA can drop rapidly and create a side-swipe risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_bicycle using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, lateral_clearance, VRU. Source case: Cyclist Lateral Avoidance Causing Close-Conflict Case.

title: Oncoming Wrong-Way Cyclist Encounter Case
text: When facing a wrong-way approaching cyclist, the vehicle should prioritize speed reduction and maintain a lateral buffer because the higher relative speed quickly compresses reaction time.
risk_mechanism: Wrong-way approach increases relative speed, making it difficult for both driver and cyclist to restore sufficient safety margin through minor trajectory adjustments.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_bicycle using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, relative_speed, lateral_clearance, VRU. Source case: Oncoming Wrong-Way Cyclist Encounter Case.

title: Fast Light-Rider Crossing Case
text: When a fast cyclist or light-mobility user crosses in front of the vehicle, prediction uncertainty should be included in risk assessment, and the vehicle should decelerate early until the conflict point is clear.
risk_mechanism: A fast light rider reaches the conflict point quickly and changes trajectory rapidly. If the vehicle judges only by current distance, it may underestimate future crossing risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_bicycle using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, prediction_uncertainty, VRU. Source case: Fast Light-Rider Crossing Case.

title: Low-Speed Close Mixed-Traffic Case in Shared Space
text: In low-speed shared spaces, close mixed-traffic risk should not be ignored just because speed is low. The vehicle should maintain low speed and actively leave space for VRU movement.
risk_mechanism: Although speed is low in shared space, VRU and vehicle paths overlap heavily, and low DCPA plus low future distance still represents contact risk.

title: Unprotected Turn Crossing Cyclist Path Case
text: When making an unprotected turn across a cyclist's path, the vehicle should complete the yielding decision before the conflict point and avoid compressing the cyclist's space by accelerating to turn first.
risk_mechanism: A turning vehicle and a straight-moving cyclist meet at the conflict point, and the vehicle's changing body orientation reduces the driver's continuous perception of lateral VRUs.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, intersection_crossing, intersection_turning_conflict using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, lateral_clearance, conflict_point, VRU. Source case: Unprotected Turn Crossing Cyclist Path Case.

title: Pedestrian Emergence from Bus Stop or Parked-Vehicle Occlusion Case
text: When there is an occlusion source on the roadside, even if the pedestrian is not fully observed, the vehicle should reduce speed and enlarge the safety margin to avoid a sudden crossing conflict from behind the occlusion.
risk_mechanism: A stopped vehicle or bus stop can occlude the pedestrian's initial position, causing the vehicle to detect the crossing target only when visible distance is insufficient and significantly compressing braking margin.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, intersection_occlusion, occluded_pedestrian_conflict using risk evidence from min_future_distance, occlusion, VRU. Source case: Pedestrian Emergence from Bus Stop or Parked-Vehicle Occlusion Case.

title: Pedestrian Sudden U-Turn Causing Prediction Failure Case
text: When a pedestrian shows clear direction reversal or stop-and-go behavior, the vehicle should extend the observation window and maintain a conservative speed to avoid secondary conflicts caused by prediction failure.
risk_mechanism: A pedestrian's sudden reversal can invalidate predictions based on short historical trajectories. If the vehicle resumes acceleration early, it may re-enter the conflict path.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for ind scenarios tagged as intersection_vru_interaction, car_pedestrian using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, prediction_uncertainty, VRU. Source case: Pedestrian Sudden U-Turn Causing Prediction Failure Case.

title: Roundabout Inner-Outer Lane Weaving Conflict Case
text: In inner-outer lane weaving areas of a roundabout, the vehicle should prioritize monitoring future conflict points and minimum distance, and avoid forced lane changes through deceleration and yielding.
risk_mechanism: Weaving between inner and outer roundabout lanes creates crossing curved trajectories. If vehicles adjust lanes or exit directions simultaneously, closest distance can decrease rapidly.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_weaving using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, conflict_point. Source case: Roundabout Inner-Outer Lane Weaving Conflict Case.

title: Roundabout Yield-Line Rolling Entry Case
text: When an entry vehicle reaches the yield line and a vehicle inside the roundabout is approaching the conflict point, it should wait for a clearly safe gap and should not force the other party to yield by rolling forward.
risk_mechanism: If an entry vehicle rolls into the roundabout without fully confirming the internal gap, it forces vehicles inside the roundabout to change speed or trajectory, creating forced-merge risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_merging using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, headway. Source case: Roundabout Yield-Line Rolling Entry Case.

title: Roundabout Exit Crosswalk Pedestrian Conflict Case
text: When pedestrians are crossing near a roundabout exit, the exiting vehicle should prioritize yielding and reduce speed to avoid a short-horizon conflict caused by accelerating at the exit.
risk_mechanism: When exiting a roundabout, the driver's attention can easily focus on the exit trajectory and rear vehicles, potentially underestimating the crossing risk of pedestrians at the exit crosswalk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vru_interaction, roundabout_exit_conflict, roundabout_exit_pedestrian_conflict using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, VRU. Source case: Roundabout Exit Crosswalk Pedestrian Conflict Case.

title: Roundabout Cyclist Priority Uncertainty Case
text: At a roundabout entry or exit, if cyclist priority is unclear, the vehicle should adopt a conservative yielding strategy and avoid entering the conflict point simultaneously with the cyclist.
risk_mechanism: When a motor vehicle and cyclist understand priority differently, both may enter the conflict point at the same time, quickly making the low-DCPA risk explicit.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vru_interaction, roundabout_cyclist_priority_uncertainty using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, conflict_point, VRU. Source case: Roundabout Cyclist Priority Uncertainty Case.

title: Roundabout Large-Vehicle Occlusion Compound-Conflict Case
text: When a large vehicle creates occlusion in a roundabout, the invisible area should be treated as a potential conflict source; the vehicle should reduce speed and wait until visibility is restored before deciding.
risk_mechanism: A large vehicle can occlude vehicles inside the roundabout, cyclists, or pedestrians, making the observable target set incomplete. Continuing to force passage can create compound conflict risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_occlusion using risk evidence from min_future_distance, prediction_uncertainty, occlusion. Source case: Roundabout Large-Vehicle Occlusion Compound-Conflict Case.

title: Roundabout Two-Stage Merging Consecutive-Conflict Case
text: Roundabout merging may involve consecutive conflict points. The vehicle should not enter using only the first small gap; it should also confirm that later conflict objects have sufficient safety margins.
risk_mechanism: After completing the first-stage merge, the entry vehicle may immediately face a second internal target. Evaluating only the nearest target can underestimate consecutive conflict risk.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_merging, roundabout_two_stage_merging using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, headway, conflict_point. Source case: Roundabout Two-Stage Merging Consecutive-Conflict Case.

title: Forced Roundabout Exit Cut-Out from Inner Lane Case
text: When a vehicle in the inner lane prepares to exit the roundabout, it should confirm a safe gap in the outer lane and delay exiting if necessary to avoid a forced cut-out.
risk_mechanism: A vehicle exiting from the inner lane must cross the outer lane. If an outer-lane vehicle is approaching and distance is insufficient, a lateral exit-cut conflict forms.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for round scenarios tagged as roundabout_vehicle_interaction, roundabout_exit_conflict, roundabout_exit_cut_across using risk evidence from DCPA, min_future_distance, headway, relative_speed, lateral_clearance. Source case: Forced Roundabout Exit Cut-Out from Inner Lane Case.

title: High-Speed Low-Gap Lane-Change Abort Case
text: Before a high-speed lane change, if the target-lane gap is insufficient and the rear vehicle has low TTC, the lane change should be aborted or delayed instead of forcing entry into the target lane.
risk_mechanism: When the rear vehicle in the target lane approaches rapidly and the available gap is insufficient, continuing the lane change forces the rear vehicle to brake hard; aborting the lane change can avoid a low-TTC conflict.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_lane_change, lane_change_abort using risk evidence from TTC, DCPA, headway, relative_speed. Source case: High-Speed Low-Gap Lane-Change Abort Case.

title: High-Speed Platoon Compression Propagation Risk Case
text: When a high-speed platoon runs with consecutive short gaps, smooth deceleration and increased following distance should be used to suppress disturbance propagation and prevent risk accumulation across multiple vehicles.
risk_mechanism: In a platoon, consecutive short headways across multiple vehicles amplify upstream deceleration disturbances, and delayed reactions by following vehicles may trigger chain hard braking or rear-end near-misses.
evidence_purpose: Supports RAG decisions for highd scenarios tagged as highway_car_following, highway_platoon_interaction, platoon_compression using risk evidence from TTC, THW, headway. Source case: High-Speed Platoon Compression Propagation Risk Case.
